english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Skid Row (downtown) and parts of South LA/Compton — avoid.
Caution around MacArthur Park and parts of downtown after dark.

hood_desc: The entertainment-industry landmark district home to the Walk of Fame, historic theaters and the Hollywood sign backdrop, touristy and uneven but iconic. Suits visitors who want the classic showbiz sights and nightlife.

A breezy beachfront city with a famous pier, wide beaches, the Third Street Promenade and an upscale, laid-back feel. Ideal for travelers wanting the ocean, walkability and easygoing California vibes.

The revitalized urban core with skyscrapers, the Arts District, historic theaters, museums and a growing dining and rooftop-bar scene. Good for those who want a dense, walkable city experience and culture.

A funky, bohemian beach neighborhood known for its boardwalk, canals, street art and quirky independent shops on Abbot Kinney. Best for creative, offbeat travelers who like beach culture with an edge.

The world-famous enclave of luxury, synonymous with Rodeo Drive shopping, palm-lined streets and celebrity glamour. Perfect for visitors seeking high-end shopping, fine dining and upscale surroundings.
lodging: HI Los Angeles Santa Monica Hostel

water.note: Tap water is treated and safe to drink throughout the city.

transit.pay: Tap a reloadable TAP card at readers on Metro Rail and buses - buy one for $2 at rail station machines or partner stores and load value or a pass; the TAP app also works by phone. Base fare is $1.75 per ride, with a $5 day-pass cap.
transit.hours: Metro Rail runs roughly 4-5am to between midnight and 2am depending on the line; there is no full 24-hour rail service.

food.name: Tacos al pastor
food.desc: Chile-marinated pork shaved off a spinning trompo, crowned with grilled pineapple and salsa. LA's defining street-corner taco, best after dark.

places.name: Leo's Tacos Truck
places.note: Trompo trucks parked at gas stations across the city; free pineapple slice on every taco, open till the small hours.

places.name: Tacos Los Guichos
places.note: Cash-only sidewalk stand named among LA's very best al pastor by L.A. TACO; go early, they sell out.

places.name: Tacos El Chido
places.note: Late-night stand near Santa Monica and Highland with char-grilled meats and generous crema.

food.name: French dip sandwich
food.desc: Roast beef, pork or lamb on a French roll dunked in pan jus. Cole's closed in 2025, so Philippe now carries the flag for LA's oldest dip.

places.name: Philippe the Original
places.note: Open since 1908, sawdust floors and communal tables; order the double-dipped beef with their famous hot mustard.

places.name: Johnny's Pastrami
places.note: Retro drive-in counter serving a pastrami dip that locals rate above the tourist landmarks.

food.name: Hand-cut pastrami on rye
food.desc: Thick, peppery, steamed pastrami carved by hand onto double-baked rye. An LA deli tradition that predates the city's taco fame.

places.name: Langer's Delicatessen
places.note: The #19 with coleslaw and Russian dressing; owners confirmed in 2025 the deli stays open through 2028 and beyond.

places.name: Wexler's Deli
places.note: House-cured and smoked pastrami at a market counter, plus excellent smoked fish plates.

places.name: Brent's Deli
places.note: Valley institution with huge portions; worth the drive if you are staying north of the hills.

food.name: Korean barbecue
food.desc: Marinated galbi and pork belly grilled at your table with a spread of banchan. Koreatown has the deepest KBBQ scene outside Seoul.

places.name: Park's BBQ
places.note: The long-standing gold standard, Michelin-listed, prime cuts and a huge banchan spread; book ahead.

places.name: Soowon Galbi
places.note: Recently promoted to Time Out's top pick; near-Park's quality at a friendlier price.

places.name: Soot Bull Jip
places.note: One of the last charcoal-grill holdouts; smoky, old-school and gloriously scruffy.

food.name: Birria tacos and burritos
food.desc: Slow-stewed beef in chile broth, tucked into griddled tortillas with cheese and a cup of consomme for dipping. LA popularised the style worldwide.

places.name: Teddy's Red Tacos
places.note: The truck that started LA's red-taco craze; secret chile consomme and shredded shoulder clod.

places.name: Burritos La Palma
places.note: Zacatecan birria burrito in a handmade flour tortilla, crisped on the plancha; a James Beard favourite.

places.name: Tacos y Birria La Unica
places.note: Neighbourhood truck turned local institution, known for quesabirria and generous consomme.

food.name: Southern Thai food
food.desc: Fiery curries, crispy catfish salad and sour southern stews. LA has the first official Thai Town in the world and cooks food you rarely find elsewhere.

places.name: Jitlada
places.note: Michelin Bib Gourmand southern Thai with a 400-item menu; try crispy morning glory salad and crab curry.

places.name: Night + Market
places.note: Kris Yenbamroong's drinking-food Thai: fried chicken, larb and natural wine in a loud, fun room.

food.name: Horchata
food.desc: Chilled rice-and-cinnamon agua fresca poured from taqueria jars all over the city. The default cooling drink alongside anything spicy.

places.name: Guisados
places.note: Family-run taqueria whose horchata is the classic pairing with their braised-stew tacos.

places.name: Gracias Madre
places.note: Plant-based Mexican with a lush, well-spiced horchata and a lovely patio.

food.name: Third-wave cold brew
food.desc: LA takes iced coffee seriously: slow-steeped cold brew and shakeratos poured in design-forward cafes across every neighbourhood.

places.name: Go Get Em Tiger
places.note: Barista-founded mini-empire; balanced, bright cold brew and an excellent almond cappuccino.

places.name: Verve Coffee Roasters
places.note: Seed-to-cup California roaster with four LA cafes and consistently clean, fruity brews.

places.name: Be Bright Coffee
places.note: US Cold Brew Championship winners; the cold brew is the reason to make the trip.

landmarks: Hollywood Sign
The white block letters on Mount Lee have symbolized the film industry and the allure of stardom since 1923, best photographed from Griffith Park's trails.
Griffith Observatory
This Art Deco observatory overlooking the city offers free telescopes, planetarium shows, and arguably the best skyline and Hollywood Sign photo vantage point in LA.
Santa Monica Pier
A classic California landmark with its Ferris wheel and amusement park perched over the Pacific, marking the historic end of Route 66.
Hollywood Walk of Fame
Thousands of bronze stars embedded along Hollywood Boulevard honor entertainment legends, drawing fans to spot their favorite celebrities' names.
TCL Chinese Theatre
This famed movie palace's forecourt, filled with handprints and footprints of Hollywood stars, has been a premiere venue and photo icon since 1927.
Getty Center
Richard Meier's hilltop museum complex combines striking modern architecture, world-class art, and manicured gardens with sweeping views across LA.
Venice Beach Boardwalk
A vibrant oceanfront strip famous for street performers, Muscle Beach, and eclectic shops that captures LA's laid-back, bohemian beach culture.
Universal Studios Hollywood
The original movie studio turned theme park lets visitors ride through blockbuster franchises and tour real working film sets.
Walt Disney Concert Hall
Frank Gehry's swirling stainless-steel facade in Downtown LA is both a striking architectural icon and home to the LA Philharmonic.
Watts Towers
Simon Rodia's soaring, mosaic-covered folk-art towers, built by hand over three decades, are a beloved and wholly unique LA landmark.

train.note: No international passenger trains serve the US West Coast. From LA Union Station, Amtrak runs the frequent Pacific Surfliner to San Diego and Santa Barbara, plus long-distance trains: Coast Starlight to the Bay Area, Portland and Seattle, Southwest Chief to Chicago, and Sunset Limited to Tucson, San Antonio and New Orleans three times a week. Metrolink commuter lines fan out to Orange County, Ventura, San Bernardino and the Antelope Valley from the same building. For Mexico, take the train or trolley to San Ysidro and cross to Tijuana on foot; sleeper space on the Chief and Starlight opens 11 months ahead.

bus.note: Cross-border buses stop at Mexican immigration on the way south - carry your passport (and check US re-entry documents for the way back), and buy an FMM tourist card at the border. Greyhound and Tufesa leave from downtown Los Angeles; you can also ride FlixBus (https://www.flixbus.com/) or Amtrak to San Diego and cross to Tijuana on foot. Domestic coaches reach Las Vegas in about five to six hours, San Francisco in eight to nine and Phoenix in seven. Everything is cheapest booked online several days ahead.

intl.to: Avalon & Two Harbors, Santa Catalina Island (USA) - departs the Catalina Sea and Air Terminal at Berth 95, San Pedro, and Catalina Landing, Long Beach

ferry.note: No international ferries operate from Los Angeles - the World Cruise Center at San Pedro handles cruise ships only. Catalina Express is the workhorse boat, crossing the 30 or so miles to Avalon in about 60-75 minutes from San Pedro, Long Beach or Dana Point, with San Pedro the only port serving Two Harbors daily. It runs year round on a fleet of eight fast vessels, but summer weekends and holidays sell out, so book ahead. Foot passengers only - you cannot take a car to Catalina.

half.name: Santa Catalina Island
half.blurb: Car-free island retreat with turquoise coves, snorkeling, and the charming harbor town of Avalon.

half.name: Palm Springs
half.blurb: Sunny desert resort town famed for mid-century architecture, palm oases, and mountain aerial tramway.

half.name: Laguna Beach
half.blurb: Artsy coastal enclave with dramatic coves, tide pools, and golden crescents of sand.

half.name: Santa Barbara
half.blurb: Spanish-style seaside city backed by mountains, with a historic mission and wine country nearby.

half.name: San Diego
half.blurb: Laid-back coastal city offering sweeping beaches, Balboa Park, and a historic old town.

full.name: Joshua Tree National Park
full.blurb: Otherworldly desert park where twisted Joshua trees meet giant boulders and dazzling night skies.
